Definition: to approach; hence, to meet in various senses
BiblicalUsage: The word means to meet, to come upon someone — and it is used for what God allows to happen: if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand, then I will appoint a place where he may flee; and the psalm promises that no evil shall befall you, neither shall any plague come near your dwelling. It is not chance — it is what God brings across your path, whether a refuge or a trouble.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for what befalls us carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the hand behind it — nothing meets me except what God has appointed, and the refuge is appointed too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
